english.title: Cause death by driving a vehicle - driver unlicensed / uninsured
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused the death of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DECEASED AND DATE OF DEATH IF DIFFERENT FROM DATE OF DRIVING..) by driving a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD..), and at that time the circumstances were such that you were committing an offence under

(A)_[section 87(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by driving the vehicle otherwise than in accordance with a licence authorising you to drive a motor vehicle of that class]_
(B)_[section 103(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by driving when you were disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle of that class]_
(C)_[section 143 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by using the vehicle when there was not in force in relation to the use of it such a policy of insurance or such a security in respect of third party risks as complied with the requirements of Part VI of the Road Traffic Act 1988]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3ZB of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) IMPORTANT NOTE - Causing death by driving a vehicle when disqualified (option [B]) is no longer covered by this offence and this option should only be selected if the offence in question took place prior to 13th April 2015. For any such offence committed after 13th April 2015, offence document H12083 (RT88530) should be used
(ii) From 1st November 2019, the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/1047) removed the current securities regime, which was used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. A two-year transitional period applied to existing securities and deposits; this meant that new securities could not be issued, however, it did not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they were valid until 1st November 2021. From 1st November 2021 compulsory motor insurance is required. See offence H100124.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the words "12 months" shall be omitted (section 61(5) Road Safety Act 2006). Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points.Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
